claude.note: Tiers are listed lightest first. Every new task names its tier with --tier: start with the lightest one that does the task well, and move up after a failure. Work that only waits needs no model (a command task, or a parked task). light, standard and complex run at xhigh effort. frontier runs Claude Fable 5.2, the strongest model, at high effort by default; --effort medium is its only other choice, and it never runs above high.

light.use: mechanical steps with nothing to judge: running tests or gates and reporting, fetching CI results or logs, spot-checks, review requests, Slack posts, routine reviewer replies, merging or enqueueing; inventories, summaries, mechanical edits

standard.use: small changes with clear done criteria and follow-on fixes; fact-gathering investigations and triage; drafting queries, permission requests and plans for a known area; a first review of a small diff; status reports; pull-request babysitting (watching, triaging wakes, fetching CI results, routine upkeep), whose code fixes resume on complex

complex.use: implementation across modules or with costly mistakes; fixing a babysitter's code or review findings; independent reviews of large or risky diffs; a failed standard attempt

frontier.use: design and difficult work: complicated or long development, an unsettled design across modules, hard investigation or root-cause analysis, verification of complicated work, a failed complex attempt. Not for routine or mechanical work, small reviews or waiting. --effort high (default) or medium, never above

codex.note: Tiers are listed lightest first; start with the lightest one that does the task well. Simple work (lookups, test runs, inventories) goes to luna or terra; hard implementation to astra. Design and the hardest work go to Claude frontier.

light.use: work with nothing to judge: running tests or gates and reporting, lookups, inventories and summaries, reproducing a bug from given steps, mechanical edits

standard.use: well-specified, bounded coding: small changes with clear done criteria, tests for existing behavior, lint or type fixes, reviews of small diffs

strong.use: bounded work that needs more judgment: live web research, reviews of medium diffs, debugging in a known area, a standard attempt that failed. Near-astra quality at a lower cost

complex.use: hard or high-risk implementation: several modules, costly or subtle mistakes, a large unfamiliar subsystem, a large or risky review, a failed strong attempt

rankNote: rank is how strong a tier's model is, on one scale for both agents. A delegated task may start tasks at its own rank or lower, never higher (start refuses it).
